The court will require a greater foundation to establish the reliability of the records. Federal Rule of Evidence 803(6) and authentication under Rule 901 call for proof that the entries were made at or near the time by someone with knowledge, that making the records was a regular practice, and that the computer process produces accurate results. Testimony that the records were kept on a regular business basis covers only part of that showing, and the defendant’s presence in court leaves both the hearsay-exception foundation and authentication still to be made.

CONFIDENCE: 86
